evidence.intree_statement: Definition sub_le (u v : SubObj x) : Type := { k : sub_dom u ~> sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ k ≈ sub_mono u }.  (* header: "The preorder on subobjects: u ≤ v when the mono of u factors through the mono of v ... a genuine preorder whose induced equivalence is exactly the setoid equivalence above." *)
Theorem sub_equiv_iff_mutual (u v : SubObj x) : (u ≈ v) ↔ (sub_le u v * sub_le v u).

Lemma sub_le_refl (u : SubObj x) : sub_le u u.  Lemma sub_le_trans (u v w : SubObj x) : sub_le u v → sub_le v w → sub_le u w.  Lemma sub_le_unique (u v : SubObj x) (k k' : sub_dom u ~> sub_dom v) : sub_mono v ∘ k ≈ sub_mono u → sub_mono v ∘ k' ≈ sub_mono u → k ≈ k'.
Lemma monic_pullback_stable {C : Category} {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (m : y ~> z) (Hm : Monic m) (P : Pullback f m) : Monic (pullback_fst f m P).
Definition monic_compose {x y z : C} {f : y ~> z} {g : x ~> y} : Monic f → Monic g → Monic (f ∘ g).

"Pulling a monomorphism back along f computes the preimage of the subobject it names; the pullback of two monomorphisms is the intersection of subobjects" — a comment in the Pullback header; no corresponding Coq construction exists.

statement_record.book: The subobjects of an object a are partially ordered by the factorization relation u ≤ v. If A has pullbacks, the pullback of two subobjects u : s → a and v : t → a is (by the preceding Lemma) a monic w : p → a with w ≤ u and w ≤ v, and it is their intersection — their meet / greatest lower bound in that partial order. More generally, for a J-indexed family of subobjects u_i : s_i → a, their wide pullback, when it exists, is their intersection. The union (join / least upper bound) of subobjects exists only under added hypotheses.
statement_record.intree: Definition sub_le (u v : SubObj x) : Type := { k : sub_dom u ~> sub_dom v & sub_mono v ∘ k ≈ sub_mono u }. ... Theorem sub_equiv_iff_mutual (u v : SubObj x) : (u ≈ v) ↔ (sub_le u v * sub_le v u). ... Lemma monic_pullback_stable ... (Hm : Monic m) (P : Pullback f m) : Monic (pullback_fst f m P).

statement_record.book: Dually to subobjects: two epis r, s with common domain a are equivalent when r = θ s for some invertible θ; the equivalence classes of such epis are the quotient objects of a, partially ordered by r ≤ s, which holds when r factors through s as r = r' s. The definition agrees with the usual notion via quotients by equivalence relations in categories where epis are onto. In Grp every quotient object of G is represented by p : G → G/N, and G/M ≤ G/N iff M contains N.

evidence.intree_statement: Record Cogenerator {C : Category} := { cog_index : Type; cog_obj : cog_index -> C; cog_separates : forall (x y : C) (f g : x ~> y), (forall (j : cog_index) (k : y ~> cog_obj j), k ∘ f ≈ k ∘ g) -> f ≈ g }.  — at C^op the field unfolds to: for f g : y ~{C}~> x, if for every j and every k : cog_obj j ~{C}~> y we have f ∘ k ≈ g ∘ k, then f ≈ g — exactly 'the family {cog_obj j} generates C'.

"such that parallel arrows [f, g : x ~> y] are equal as soon as they agree after every arrow [k : y ~> cog_obj j] into a member of the family. Equivalently the representables [C(-, cog_obj j)] are jointly faithful. This is the minimal data form of 'cogenerating family'."

statement_record.book: A set S of objects of C generates C when for every parallel pair h ≠ h' : c → d there exist s ∈ S and f : s → c with h f ≠ h' f. (Mac Lane remarks 'separates' would have been the better term.) The single-object case s generates C is included. Examples: the one-point set generates Set; Z generates Ab and Grp; R generates R-Mod; the finite cyclic groups generate the finite (and the torsion) abelian groups.
statement_record.intree: Record Cogenerator {C : Category} := { cog_index : Type; cog_obj : cog_index -> C; cog_separates : forall (x y : C) (f g : x ~> y), (forall (j : cog_index) (k : y ~> cog_obj j), k ∘ f ≈ k ∘ g) -> f ≈ g }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the DUAL notion is defined. `Cogenerator` is universe-polymorphic in {C : Category}, and `Cogenerator (C^op)` is definitionally the generating-family condition (precomposition by arrows out of family members separates parallel arrows), so the mathematical content is one op-instantiation away — but no in-tree definition, name, instance, or consequence of a generating set exists. Note also the constructive rephrasing: the in-tree field is the contrapositive/positive form (agreement everywhere implies equality) rather than Mac Lane's 'h ≠ h' implies some f distinguishes them'; that is the faithful constructive reading, not a weakening.
